audit_findings.title: Recurring acquisitions may be uncharged reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $249.682 million of acquisition cash spending in 2023-2025; computed three-year average $83.227 million annually, equal to 26.4% of the $315.4 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and growth; acquired earnings enter historical OE while any maintenance-like acquisition spending is absent from reinvestment
audit_findings.evidence: Our programmatic acquisitions, which most often “fill white space” within our ecosystem, add their value principally by enhancing our platform comprehensiveness, and accordingly we consider this programmatic aspect of our growth as characteristically within our mainstream business performance (unlike platform acquisitions).
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that programmatic acquisitions are recurring and treated as mainstream growth, but do not establish that they are required maintenance spending. That characterization remains unresolved. Nevertheless, the three-year spending rate is large relative to anchor OE and could materially reduce distributable OE, scenario values, and the buy-below price if even a substantial portion is maintenance-like.
audit_findings.action: Classify each 2023-2025 acquisition as maintenance-like or optional growth, quantify acquired OE and organic growth separately, and rerun the valuation with the supported recurring acquisition charge deducted from OE.

audit_findings.title: Cash-settled DCP liability is missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $117.423 million at 2026-06-30; computed $0.36 per diluted share and 2.6% of $4.578 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: equity bridge; the cash-settled obligation is a claim senior to common equity
audit_findings.evidence: DCP participants’ holdings in phantom investment funds are classified as liabilities in either Accruals and other current liabilities or Deferred compensation plan liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets as they will be settled in cash upon eventual distribution.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the latest filing reports a $117.423 million cash-settled DCP liability, while the bridge deducts none of it. Deducting it would reduce base value from approximately $14.22 to $13.86 per share. That is small relative to the $19.49 gap between base value and the $33.71 market price and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge with a $117.423 million deduction, verify that no dedicated offsetting plan assets exist, and retain only share-settled DCP phantom shares in the denominator.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $146.981 million, computed $0.46 per diluted share and 3.2% of $4.578 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: equity bridge; non-excess cash should not be added to operating value
audit_findings.evidence: CSS balances not utilized for eligible products or services may roll over to future periods or are refundable.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that CSS deposits were $496.322 million, exceeding total cash of $146.981 million, but it does not establish how much cash is legally or operationally reserved for those deposits. Even the conservative removal of the entire cash addition would lower base value only from approximately $14.22 to $13.77 per share, still far below the $33.71 market price. The conclusion therefore does not depend on resolving the excess-cash amount.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by jurisdiction against refundable CSS deposits, deferred revenue obligations, taxes, and minimum operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only the demonstrably distributable remainder.

audit_findings.title: Convertible shares and retained interest describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 6.908797 million conversion shares, 2.15% of the 321.842636 million denominator; removing them while retaining interest raises computed base value by about $0.32 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: shares and OE numerator; conversion shares dilute value while retained note interest reduces OE
audit_findings.evidence: To compute the numerator of diluted net income per share attributable to Bentley Systems stockholders , interest expense, net of tax, attributable to the assumed conversion of the convertible senior notes using the if‑converted method is added back to basic net income attributable to Bentley Systems .
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is demonstrably inconsistent because the valuation includes the 2027-note conversion shares while retaining the related interest expense. Under the stated equity-OE debt treatment, removing those shares would raise base value to approximately $14.54 per share. The increase is far too small to close the gap to the $33.71 market price and does not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using one coherent convention: preferably retain note interest and remove 6.908797 million conversion shares, or alternatively add back the filed after-tax interest and model conversion and capped-call settlement consistently.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized operating expenditures may bypass OE reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: OE; cash additions capitalized outside reported investing capex may escape the reinvestment deduction while later amortization is added back
audit_findings.evidence: Certain implementation costs are capitalized and included in Prepaid and other current assets or Other assets in the consolidated balance sheets, depending on the short- or long-term nature of such costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate capitalized internal-use implementation and contract-obtainment assets, but the supplied record does not show the gross cash additions by year or whether the OE calculation already captures them through operating cash flow. An OE error is therefore possible rather than demonstrated, and its materiality cannot be established from the available balances and amortization alone.
audit_findings.action: Obtain annual rollforwards and cash additions for internal-use software implementation costs and capitalized contract costs for 2020-2025; map them to operating cash flow and the OE worksheet, then rerun OE subtracting omitted additions without double-counting amortization.

audit_findings.title: Noncash swap marks may remain in the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed pretax fair-value changes: $5.038 million loss in 2023, $0.010 million gain in 2024, and $10.238 million loss in 2025; the 2025 amount is 3.2% of the $315.4 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE anchor; noncash fair-value gains or losses distort annual OE and the fitted log trend, while actual swap receipts belong with financing cost
audit_findings.evidence: Gain (loss) from the change in fair value and payments related to the interest rate swap are recognized in Other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations (see Note 20).
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate noncash swap marks, but the supplied valuation method does not confirm whether they were removed and the record lacks the 2020-2022 marks needed to determine the full trend effect. The known amounts are modest relative to anchor OE, but the total effect on the six-year log trend remains unresolved. Gains would overstate and losses would understate value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect each 2020-2025 OE worksheet, remove the filed noncash swap fair-value change while retaining actual swap receipts or payments consistently with interest expense, and recompute the OE series, trend anchor, and scenarios.
